reasoning_evidence: Reported COD 2028-01-01 has zero queue-history drift across 18 monthly snapshots (2025-01 to 2026-06) — but zero drift on a pre-IA project with no downstream milestones is not achievement evidence, it is placeholder stability
No signed IA on file with ERCOT (iaSigned null through 2026-06-01); typical Oncor IA negotiation post-FIS runs 9-15 months, and Amendment 1 typically adds another 6-12 months of schedule slip

No confirmed turbine OEM order: Aug 2024 press ('discussions ongoing with leading manufacturer') is the most recent public signal, and no announcement has surfaced through 2026-07. Heavy-frame simple-cycle CTGs (F/H/HA class, ~450 MW each) have firm-order-to-delivery lead times of 3-5 years — a Jan 2028 COD would require a PO already in place

No visible construction as of 2026-06-01, 18 months into permit validity and 6 months before reported COD; 900 MW simple-cycle greenfield builds require 24-36 months of visible on-site work (grading, foundations, turbine hall, cooling infrastructure)

Capacity bumped 900 MW → 1036 MW in the ERCOT queue Aug 2025 without a matching TCEQ permit amendment (permit still authorizes 900 MW combined via two CTGs) — either a paper capacity increase in the queue only or a pending permit revision that will add lead time
TCEQ permit issued 2024-12-20 via streamlined EGU Standard Permit path (30 TAC 116.602, 1-day turnaround) rather than full NSR — permit exists but does not imply construction readiness

Positive signals that keep the verdict 'real_early' not 'paper': permit is issued to a real, named entity with a real address at a real greenfield location; engineered emissions controls (SCR + CEMS) specified with numeric limits; developer EmberClear has two prior US plants (Birdsboro PA operating, Lincoln Land IL announced) rather than a first-time speculator; gas supply arrangement named with counterparty and pipeline
Reasonable build path: IA signed 2027, turbine PO firm 2027, mobilization 2028, in-service 2030-2031
